entries.content_plain: CHAPTER 47 Is 47:1-15 . The Destruction of Babylon Is Represented under the Image of a Royal Virgin Brought Down in a Moment from Her Magnificent Throne to the Extreme of Degradation. 1. in the dust-- (See on Is 3:26 ; Job 2:13 ; La 2:10 ). virgin-- that is, heretofore uncaptured [Herodotus, 1.191]. daughter of Babylon-- Babylon and its inhabitants (see on Is 1:8 ; Is 37:22 ). no throne-- The seat of empire was transferred to Shushan. Alexander intended to have made Babylon his seat of empire, but Providence defeated his design. He soon died; and Seleucia, being built near, robbed it of its inhabitants, and even of its name, which was applied to Seleucia. delicate-- alluding to the effeminate debauchery and prostitution of all classes at banquets and religious rites [Curtius, 5.1; Herodotus, 1.199; Baruch, 6.43].

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9227"/><div sID="gen15746" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9227"/><hi type="bold">2. millstones--</hi>like the querns or hand-mills, found in this country, before the invention of water mills and windmills: a convex stone, made by the hand to turn in a concave stone, fitted to receive it, the corn being ground between them: the office of a female slave in the East; most degrading (<reference osisRef="Job.31.10">Job 31:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="Matt.24.41">Mt 24:41</reference>).<div eID="gen15746" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15747" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">uncover thy locks--</hi>rather, "take off thy veil" [Horsley]: perhaps the removal of the plaited hair worn round the women's temples is included; it, too, is a covering (<reference osisRef="1Cor.11.15">1Co 11:15</reference>); to remove it and the veil is the badge of the lowest female degradation; in the East the head is the seat of female modesty; the face of a woman is seldom, the whole head almost never, seen bare (see on <reference osisRef="Isa.22.8">Is 22:8</reference>).<div eID="gen15747" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15748" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">make bare the leg--</hi>rather "lift up (literally, 'uncover'; as in lifting up the train the leg is uncovered) thy flowing train." In Mesopotamia, women of low rank, as occasion requires, wade across the rivers with stript legs, or else entirely put off their garments and swim across. entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9228"/><div sID="gen15750" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9228"/><hi type="bold">3. not meet ... as a man--</hi>rather, "I will not meet a man," that is, suffer man to intercede with me--give man an audience [Horsley]. Or, "I will not make peace with any man," before all are destroyed. Or else from striking the victims sacrificed in making treaties. <div eID="gen15750" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9231"/><div sID="gen15755" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9231"/>6. reason for God's vengeance on Babylon: in executing God's will against His people, she had done so with wanton cruelty (<reference osisRef="Isa.10.5">Is 10:5</reference>, &c.; <reference osisRef="Jer.50.17">Jr 50:17</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.51.33">51:33</reference>; <reference osisRef="Zech.1.15">Zec 1:15</reference>).<div eID="gen15755" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15756" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">polluted my inheritance--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Isa.43.28">Is 43:28</reference>).<div eID="gen15756" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15757" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">the ancient--</hi>Even old age was disregarded by the Chaldeans, who treated all alike with cruelty (<reference osisRef="Lam.4.16">La 4:16</reference>; <reference osisRef="Lam.5.12">5:12</reference>) [Rosenmuller]. Or, "the ancient" means Israel, worn out with calamities in the latter period of its history (<reference osisRef="Isa.46.4">Is 46:4</reference>), as its earlier stage of history is called its "youth" (<reference osisRef="Isa.54.6">Is 54:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ezek.16.60">Eze 16:60</reference>). <div eID="gen15757" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 6. reason for God's vengeance on Babylon: in executing God's will against His people, she had done so with wanton cruelty ( Is 10:5 , &c.; Jr 50:17 ; 51:33 ; Zec 1:15 ). polluted my inheritance-- ( Is 43:28 ). the ancient-- Even old age was disregarded by the Chaldeans, who treated all alike with cruelty ( La 4:16 ; 5:12 ) [Rosenmuller]. Or, "the ancient" means Israel, worn out with calamities in the latter period of its history ( Is 46:4 ), as its earlier stage of history is called its "youth" ( Is 54:6 ; Eze 16:60 ).

Babylon was famous for "expiations or sacrifices, and other incantations, whereby they tried to avert evil and obtain good" [Diodorus Siculus]. <div eID="gen15765" type="x-p"/>
